title: Tenant request inbox and durable chunk-store hardening

phases.objective: List tenant tickets and resolution cases as one bounded inbox while retaining independent statuses, enforcing object-level tenant scope, and degrading large tool responses safely when durable chunk schema is incomplete.

e2e_journeys.actor: platform admin or authenticated tenant member
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: A bounded ticket/case projection and redacted timeline are returned, while incomplete chunk persistence falls back to bounded inline output or a typed budget error instead of failing the request process.
steps: Authorize the caller against platform-admin or active tenant membership scope.
Detect whether the explicit tenant_resolution_cases.ticket_id link is available and preserve the ticket:// compatibility fallback before migration.
Discover a bounded candidate ticket window from set-wise ticket, event, case, and readback activity sources before exact ordering.
Read tickets ordered by latest activity and stable ticket_id with opaque cursor pagination.
Return ticket status and resolution case status in separate nested objects.
Read ticket, case, and readback timeline rows with tenant-safe redaction and bounded row limits.
Inspect durable chunk-store schema before persistence and return bounded inline output when required columns are unavailable.
Apply the caller's effective client and envelope response budget to degraded system-tool responses.
Resolve the central tenant User JWT middleware to the same userJwtAuth contract declared by OpenAPI.
Expose the four inbox endpoints through the generated frontend dispatch inventory.
assertions: Ticket open and resolution case escalated remain separate states for the regression ticket.
A tenant cannot read another tenant's request by tenant_id, ticket_id, or resolution_case_id inference.
Cursor pagination uses latest_activity_at plus ticket_id and never OFFSET.
Latest-activity ranking performs exact correlated calculations only for a bounded candidate ticket window.
Tenant timelines exclude internal ticket events, case evidence refs, and raw readback states.
The migration is additive and does not delete, archive, or rename existing records.
Chunk schema failures expose typed non-secret diagnostics and do not silently drop the tool-list request.
Default client budgets reject oversized degraded system-tool lists with a typed 503, while an explicit sufficient bounded budget preserves a 200 response.
Generated dispatch classifies both tenant request routes as user_jwt with equivalent OpenAPI authentication.
The generated dispatch inventory contains the admin and tenant request list/detail surfaces.

phases.objective: Provide schema readiness views, typed diagnostics, bounded paging, stable request identifiers, explicit authentication parity, and explicit response-budget behavior without external mutations.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Migration readiness views, inbox list filters, and system-tool list routes
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Operations can distinguish missing schema from missing data, bound latest-activity work, verify authentication parity, and receive a bounded response or typed budget failure.
steps: Inspect explicit ticket-link and chunk-runtime schema readiness.
List a bounded page with filters and a stable next cursor.
Bound exact latest-activity calculations to a candidate ticket set.
Verify runtime User JWT evidence matches the tenant inbox OpenAPI security contract.
Apply the effective client and envelope budget to degraded system-tool list responses.
Log only error code, cause code, operation, request id, and source tool key during chunk fallback.
assertions: No response content or credentials are written to fallback diagnostics.
Readiness views report blocked until every required additive column and index is present.
Candidate activity indexes support ticket lifecycle, resolution-case event, and readback discovery.
Both tenant request routes have resolved user_jwt runtime authentication and equivalent userJwtAuth OpenAPI security.
An oversized degraded response is returned as a typed non-secret 503 rather than an unhandled rejection.
No migration is applied by the runtime code in this change.

phases.objective: Fail closed on authorization, malformed cursors, unbounded activity work, unresolved authentication evidence, and response-budget overflow while retaining bounded inline availability during chunk-store schema drift.

e2e_journeys.actor: unauthorized tenant caller or runtime with incomplete chunk schema
e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Tenant request detail lookup, inbox list ranking, or governed response chunk persistence
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Unauthorized object access is rejected, latest-activity work remains bounded, authentication evidence remains explicit, and chunk persistence degradation is contained without exposing secrets.
steps: Attempt to access a tenant request without an active membership.
Attempt to decode a malformed pagination cursor.
Discover latest-activity candidates from bounded set-wise sources.
Verify the central User JWT middleware remains statically resolvable by generated dispatch governance.
Inspect a chunk table missing one runtime-required ownership column.
Attempt to return a degraded response that exceeds the effective client budget.
Return typed errors or bounded inline response without provider calls.
assertions: Unauthorized tenant access returns tenant_request_scope_violation.
Malformed cursors return tenant_request_cursor_invalid.
Candidate discovery is capped and exact ordering is restricted to candidate ticket IDs.
The tenant inbox route guard is resolved as user_jwt rather than unknown auth evidence.
Missing chunk columns are listed explicitly with secrets_included=false.
Budget overflow returns response_chunk_persistence_unavailable_inline_limit_exceeded with secrets_included=false.
No external provider call, SQL apply, or destructive mutation occurs.

phases.objective: Apply the additive migration in an authorized non-production database and verify the regression ticket appears first with open/escalated states.
Verify exact Production SHA, migration ledger, schema readback, and live tenant/admin inbox responses.
